Hmm, this is getting complicated. Let's think.

Actually x13 = pair(x9, x12) where x9 = combine((identity,rot90),(rot180,rot270)) = (identity, rot90, rot180, rot270). x12 = combine((identity,rot270),(rot180,rot90)) = (identity, rot270, rot180, rot90).

So x13 = pair of these two tuples: ((identity,rot90,rot180,rot270),(identity,rot270,rot180,rot90)). 4 pairs.

x16 = chain(first, x14, x15): x15(x) = {first(x)}; x14 = lambda y: rapply(y, I)? Wait x14 = rbind(rapply, I) => lambda functions: rapply(functions, I). So x14(x15(x)) applies each function in {first(x)} to I, giving {first(x)(I)}. Then first => first(x)(I).

Then x17 = compose(x6, x16) = lambda x: x6(first(x)(I)).

x6 = fork(both, x2, x5) = lambda x: both(x2(x), x5(x)). x5 = fork(greater, x3, x4): x3(x) = size(dedupe(first(x))), x4(x) = size(dedupe(last(x))). Hmm first/last of grid? first(I) = first row (tuple), last(I) = last row.

Wait x16 gives first(x)(I) which is a transformed grid, then x6 evaluates on that grid. x2 checks horizontal frontier exists, x5 = greater(x3,x4): size(dedupe(first row)) > size(dedupe(last row))? Hmm.

x18 = extract(x13, x17): find pair (a,b) in x13 such that x17(pair)? x16 = chain(first, x14, x15). Actually these are defined inside verify function, so closures capture I. Yes! I is available. So x14 = rbind(rapply, I) = lambda functions: rapply(functions, I). rapply applies each function to I.

So x16(p) = first(rapply({first(p)}, I)) = first(p)(I) where first(p) = first tuple of the pair. Then x6 applied: x17(p) = x6(first(p)(I)).

Hmm so first(p) is a tuple like (identity, rot90, rot180, rot270). first(p)(I) means calling first(p) as a function with argument I? But first(p) is a tuple, not callable. Wait chain(first, x14, x15): inner f = x15, then g = x14, then h = first. So x16(p) = first(x14(x15(p))).

x15(p) = initset(first(p)) = frozenset({first(p)}) — first(p) is the first element of pair p, which is a tuple of functions. So set contains one tuple.

x13 = pair(x9, x12). pair(a,b) = tuple(zip(a,b)). x9 has 4 elements, x12 has 4 elements. zip gives ((identity,identity),(rot90,rot270),(rot180,rot180),(rot270,rot90)). So x13 is a tuple of 4 pairs! Not a pair of tuples. Good.

first(g) = first row, dedupe gives unique colors in order, size = number distinct. last(g) = last row, size distinct.

So condition: x2: there's at least one horizontal-line frontier (a row or column all same). And x5: distinct colors in first row > distinct colors in last row.
